title: Grok adapter: run roles on the grok CLI as a third vendor
lead: ork runs a role round on the `grok` CLI like it runs `claude` and `codex`: a new `internal/agent/grok` package, a Grok runner in the daemon, `grok` accepted wherever a vendor is named, and the grok column of the design table filled from real probes. It is not the default for any role: the owner adds Grok rows to the matrix as alternates.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner decisions: 2026-10-28 (the adapter supports any role; Grok is an alternate matrix row, never the default; rule u2 still bars a cross-vendor reviewer unless the owner asks), 2026-10-30 (the implementer may run the six probes in `spike/grok.sh` once on or after 2026-11-01, stops on any HTTP 403 "used all available credits" with no retry loop, uses the vendor CLI's own login and never reads credential files), 2026-10-31 (S72 moves to v1.1). Grok credits reset on 2026-11-01, so the probe step stays as the S72 spec says, and nothing here may start before that date. No dependency is added.

Re-anchored at HEAD (2026-10-31):
- `internal/agent` has `claude` and `codex` only. `codex` is one file of code plus `fixture.go` (`internal/agent/codex/codex.go`: `Spec`, `Args`, `ParseLine`, `Run`; `fixture.go`: candidates, `vendor.fixture-candidates`); `claude` splits the same work over `args.go`, `classify.go`, `report.go`, `run.go`, `stream.go`, `types.go`. Both start the process in its own process group, report the pgid through `OnStart`, kill the group when the context ends (`internal/clirun`, `code.process-groups`, adj 79), call `OnEvent` for each stream line, and return an error only when a cancel killed the process.
- The engine-facing runners are in `internal/daemon/runner.go`: `claudeRunner` (`:21-84`, vendor check at `:28`), `vendorRunner` (`:87`) with `supportsVendor` (`:89`: `claude` or `codex`) and a switch that refuses any other vendor with "unsupported vendor" (`:90-99`), and `codexRunner` (`:101-137`). They are wired in `internal/daemon/runs.go:188-191`. A matrix row reaches an adapter through `matrixAdapters` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:336-337`, keyed on the row's `agent`, adj 155), used when a plan is built (`runs.go:417,436`) and by `matrixUse` (`internal/daemon/matrix.go`). The old spec's "plan takes the first row whose vendor is claude, hard-coded at :224" is gone: plans are already adapter-aware, so Grok needs a table entry, not a planning change. A launch override is checked by `supportsVendor` (`runs.go:461`); `ork vendor out|back` by `supportsVendor` (`internal/daemon/vendors.go:59-60`) and by `vendorNames` and a literal test (`internal/cli/vendor.go:15,70`).
- The watchdog (`internal/engine/watchdog.go:14-24`) kills a role that sends no event and no text for 30 minutes. A Grok role that uses `--output-format json` sends nothing until it ends, and would be killed at 30 minutes. The adapter must call `OnEvent` for each line of a streaming output (`--output-format streaming-messages-json --include-partial-messages`, probe 02), unless the probes show it cannot.
- `testdata/vendors/grok/` holds the S01 results from before the credits ran out: probes 01, 02, 04 and 05 reached the API and got HTTP 403 (`01-plain-json.stdout`: "used all available credits or reached its monthly spending limit", `http_status` 403); 03 used a team id as a session id by mistake; 06 is the bad-model message ("Couldn't set model ... unknown model id"). That 403 is a real sample, so the quota stop can be classified now (`vendor.unsampled-classes`, adj 77, bars only synthetic rules). Out of credits is `engine.ExitOutOfCredits`; codex maps its text to it the same way (`internal/agent/codex/codex.go`, `TestOutOfCreditsHasItsOwnClassification`).
- The init event of probe 02 lists grok's tool names (`read_file`, `write`, `search_replace`, `run_terminal_command`, `grep`, `list_dir`, ...), so `--tools Read` in probe 04 was probably a wrong name (`docs/design.md:1039-1041`). `--permission-mode` takes `default, acceptEdits, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, plan`; `--reasoning-effort`, `--resume ID`, `--sandbox PROFILE` and `--cwd` exist (`testdata/vendors/grok/help-excerpt.txt`).
- `ork doctor` already lists `grok` (path and `--version`, optional: `internal/cli/doctor.go:392`, `internal/cli/cli.go:135`). A login line is not there for any vendor. `grok models` prints "You are not authenticated." while a `-p` call still reached the API with auth source `oauth` (`docs/design.md:1030-1034`), so it is not a reliable login test.
- The docs say grok has no adapter in several places: `docs/design.md:181-185` (a runnable vendor is `claude` or `codex`), `:789-812` (the vendor table; most of the grok column is *unverified*), `:1030-1041` (Grok auth, Grok is not measured), `docs/guide.md:60` and `:192`, `internal/cli/cli.go:112` (usage text), `docs/diagrams.md:30`. `docs/boundaries.md:69` and `docs/glossary.md:79` already name `grok`.

What is not decided and is listed for the owner in the manifest: the matrix `agent` value for Grok rows, how write roles run (tool names with a permission mode, or a sandbox profile as codex does), the slot cap, and the login line in doctor. The steps below stop and report rather than guess on the write mode.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Before the probes (they use the real 403 and bad-model results already in the tree):
- `TestGrokCreditsStopClassifiesAsOutOfCredits` (`internal/agent/grok`): the 403 `error` line of `testdata/vendors/grok/01-plain-json.stdout`, with exit 1, classifies as out of credits, not a rate limit. Fails first: no package.
- `TestGrokBadModelAndAuthStayUnclassified`: the bad-model result (`06-bad-model.stdout`, exit 1) is `unclassified`, and an unauthenticated message is `unclassified` (adj 77).
- `TestGrokArgsRefuseFlagLikeInputs`: a prompt or resume id starting with `-` is refused, as `TestCodexArgsRefuseFlagLikeInputs` does.
- `TestGrokRunUsesItsOwnProcessGroupAndKillsItOnCancel`, `TestGrokReportsThePGIDThroughOnStart` and `TestGrokCancellationAndMissingBinary`: follow the codex tests with a fake `grok` binary (see `TestMain` in `internal/agent/codex/codex_test.go`).
- `TestGrokCallsOnEventForEachStreamLine`: each line of a streamed fixture reaches `OnEvent`, so the watchdog sees a live role.
- Daemon: `TestDaemonRunnerDispatchesByVendor` takes `grok` to the Grok runner and another name (say `acme`) to "unsupported vendor"; `TestRunPlanAcceptsGrokOverride`; `TestMatrixAdaptersMapTheGrokAgent` (`matrixUse` says `used as grok` for the agent value chosen in the manifest, case-insensitive); `TestVendorOutAndBackAcceptGrok` (`internal/daemon`, `internal/cli`); the two unsupported-vendor cases in `runs_test.go` use another name.
- A plan whose recommendation is a Claude row with a Grok alternate keeps both, in that order: `TestPlanKeepsAGrokAlternateAfterTheRecommendedRow`. Grok is never first unless the matrix recommends it.

After the probes succeed (fixtures are real output):
- `TestGrokParsesAPlainJSONFixtureWithUsage`: `01-plain-json.stdout` gives a result with non-zero usage and a session id.
- `TestGrokResumesByARealSessionID`: `03-resume-by-id` carries the session id of probe 01 and its command line (`.cmd`) shows `--resume ID`.
- `TestGrokReadOnlyToolNameComesFromTheFixture`: the tool name in the allowlist probe (04) is the one `Args` passes, taken from the fixture (`read_file` or `Read`).
- `TestGrokReadOnlyRoleUsesPlanMode` and, for write roles, a test for the mode chosen in Implement step 4.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Do not start before 2026-11-01. Tests that need only the existing 403 and bad-model results may be written earlier.

1. Probes. Run `spike/grok.sh PROBE_REPO RAW_DIR FIXTURE_DIR` once, with the probe repo and raw directory under `.scratch/` of the main checkout. Use the CLI's own login; read no credential file; no retry loop. If probe 01 or any probe returns the 403 again, stop and report to the orchestrator with the log; do not write the adapter against synthetic output. Replace the 01-06 results in `testdata/vendors/grok/` with the redacted real output (`spike/common.zsh` redacts; check the output for team ids and tokens before it is kept) and attach the probe log to the report. Probe 04 uses the real tool name from probe 02's init event (edit `spike/grok.sh` for that one line).
2. Tests first, from the lists above. The first group does not need the probes.
3. Adapter, on the codex and claude shape: command line (`-p PROMPT`, `-m MODEL`, `--reasoning-effort`, `--cwd`, `--resume ID`, output format from probe 02 so that events stream), result with usage and session id from the fixtures, the report file taking precedence as in the other adapters, candidates saved for rounds that are not ok (`vendor.fixture-candidates`), out-of-credits and everything else per the tests. Add no dependency.
4. Permissions. Read-only roles use `--permission-mode plan` (probe 05 shows whether plan mode refused the edit). Write roles: the allowlist of `engine.Request.Allowlist` holds claude-style patterns that `--tools` (names only) cannot express, and probe 04 only measures a name list with `dontAsk`. Take the write-role flags from what probes 04 and 05 showed. If they do not show a mode that keeps a write role inside its worktree, stop and report to the orchestrator; the owner decides (see the manifest). Do not use `bypassPermissions` and do not guess.
5. Daemon and CLI: the `grokRunner`, `supportsVendor`, the `vendorRunner` case, the wiring, the `matrixAdapters` entry, the messages and usage text listed in Files. `defaultVendorCaps` stays as it is (no Grok cap). Leave Grok unreachable as a default: no code makes it a first choice; the plan follows the matrix.
6. Doctor: it already reports `grok` on PATH with its version. Add a login line only if a probe shows a command that reports login state without a model call; otherwise change nothing and say so in the report. Never read credential files.
7. Docs: the grok column of `docs/design.md:789-812` is filled from the probes (each cell cites a fixture or says *unverified*), `:181-185` and `:1030-1041` are updated, `docs/guide.md:60,192` and `docs/diagrams.md:30` say that ork runs `claude`, `codex` and `grok`. Mark the adapter behavior *proposed* until an adj record decides the write mode.
8. The matrix rows are not edited by the implementer. Put the exact `slicer relay-roles add` commands in the report (an implementer alternate after r9 for a whole slice, and the reviewer, gate and UI alternates the owner may pick), with the model and reasoning names taken from `models.txt` and the probes, and the agent value the manifest settles. The owner adds them at landing.
9. `CHANGELOG.md`: one entry under `## Unreleased`, added last. Do not touch the engine, the watchdog, `internal/clirun`, or other vendors' adapters. UI slice (CLI text): UI pass (r14).

sections.body:

- `go vet ./...`

- `adj lint --root /Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork`
- A probe re-run log in the report (or the stop report with the 403).
- `rg -n "grok" docs/design.md docs/guide.md` shows no remaining "no adapter" statement.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] The owner adds the Grok matrix rows with the reported commands, runs `ork vendor out grok` and `ork vendor back grok`, and runs one low-risk role on a Grok row (for example a reviewer on a small slice, chosen by the owner) to see a live tail, tokens and a clean exit. Not before the daemon is rebuilt and restarted.
